---
title: "Pre-processing workflow"
description: "Use source-aware transformation, imputation and normalization with explicit method choices and before/after processing reports."
---

## Shared workflow

After Search/import has produced a real protein-by-sample matrix, the GUI presents:

**Within-group Processing → Data Transformation → Data Imputation → Data Normalization**

Schema v4 appends every successful stage as a new run. The active matrix advances through the workflow, while prior matrix states remain recoverable.

## Source-aware defaults

ProtVis 0.9.1 can resolve **Auto (source recommended)** settings. For MaxQuant, the archived-compatible preset is:

**replicate correction → log2(intensity × 1e7) → kNN (GUI seed 12345; engine defaults also apply) → sample-median normalization + historical row shift**

For other sources, defaults are more conservative and can be changed explicitly in the module.

## 1. Within-group Processing

Within-group Processing performs replicate-aware correction when `_1/_2/_3` sample suffixes are available, removes all-zero proteins in that replicate workflow, and safely collapses duplicated protein IDs before reshaping. If recognizable replicate suffixes are absent, the validated matrix is retained without forcing replicate correction.

The dropdown also offers **Replicate filtering (at least two detected)** with optional group mean filling, unchecked by default.

Read [Within-group Processing](correct_noise.qmd).

## 2. Data Transformation

The current menu includes **Auto (source recommended)**, **MaxQuant: log2(x × 1e7)**, **log2**, **None**, **log10**, plus advanced Z-score/scale/center options. The transformation method is stored with the project. Establish the matrix scale before choosing normalization.

Read [Data transformation](data_transformed.qmd).

## 3. Data Imputation

The current GUI offers **kNN**, **RF**, **Mean**, **Median**, and **Minimum**. It no longer exposes Zero or MinProb/q controls. A **Random seed** is explicit (default `12345`) so stochastic/reproducibility-sensitive methods can be repeated.

Read [Data imputation](data_imputation.qmd).

## 4. Data Normalization

The verified GUI supports sample median subtraction and a source-aware archived positive-shift preset. See the method-specific chapter for formulas, assumptions and reporting.

Read [Data normalization](data_normalization.qmd).

## Important change for differential analysis

::: {.callout-important}
### Imputation is not the default inferential input
**Recommended DEP** deliberately uses **Step4 transformed data before the dedicated Imputation module**, which may already contain filling from Within-group Processing, then applies its own sample-median centering and detection filter. Step5/Step6 remain important for complete-matrix visualization, QC and analyses that explicitly require imputed/normalized data, but they do not force imputed values into the default DEP model.
:::

Before downstream analysis, inspect [Project Dashboard](../reproducibility/Project_Dashboard.qmd) and confirm the current/active run, sample mapping, missingness and workflow validity.

## Reporting each stage

Open **Processing report** after completing a saved run. The chapters explain which counts reflect filling, masking, removal or a scale change. Record the resolved method and input/output scale; changes in missing percentage or distribution alone do not prove improved biological validity.
